subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add `models.providers.<provider>.enabled?: boolean` as a core config contract for temporarily disabling configured model providers?
rationale: Root policy sets a high bar for new config/default surfaces, and this flag would affect provider routing, generated catalogs, fallback behavior, auth/probe visibility, and operator status output.

options.title: Approve provider flag
options.body: Add the config flag with default-enabled behavior and require complete runtime/status/docs/test coverage before implementation.

options.title: Prefer existing config removal
options.body: Keep the current model where disabling a provider means removing or moving the provider block, avoiding another core config option.

options.title: Use a different control surface
options.body: Ask for a narrower provider/runtime control such as status-only warnings or a doctor-assisted temporary removal flow instead of a persistent enabled flag.

recommendation.title: Approve provider flag
recommendation.body: Add the config flag with default-enabled behavior and require complete runtime/status/docs/test coverage before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available signal from the prior issue review and recent provider/config/runtime history, though the implementation surface is shared.
